headline: A PwC survey finds Singapore workers use AI at work more than workers worldwide, yet fewer of them feel secure in their jobs than two years ago.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: fresh, well-sampled survey with clear figures, but it is self-reported opinion data with no decision or event behind it.
importance_line: What changed is that heavy AI use in Singapore has come with a 15-point drop in job-security confidence since 2024 while the global figure held steady, which matters first to workers, then to employers and unions, but the data is self-reported by 1,000 local respondents and does not show that AI caused the drop.
summary: The Business Times reports, citing PwC's Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey 2026, that 74 percent of Singapore respondents used AI at work in the past year against 64 percent globally, while the share moderately to extremely confident about their job security over the next 12 months fell to 69 percent from 84 percent in 2024, as the global figure held at 84 percent. The Singapore results draw on 1,000 local respondents out of 49,364 workers in 48 territories surveyed in May and June 2026, and PwC Singapore signed an agreement the same day with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), Singapore's national trade union centre, to help companies create better jobs as they adopt AI.
notes: Full text read. Figures are PwC's, as given by The Business Times; PwC's own release was not opened. The NTUC description is general background, not from the article.
